question: Should Discord subagent progress become states within the canonical status-reaction controller, or remain a separate tracker with enforced disjoint emoji configuration?
rationale: Both approaches can fix the immediate defect, but they establish different permanent ownership, configuration, lifecycle, and compatibility contracts that automation should not choose implicitly.

options.title: Extend status controller
options.body: Use the canonical serialized source-message owner for subagent count, failure, and typing lifecycle alongside existing queued, thinking, tool, done, and error states.

options.title: Enforce disjoint configuration
options.body: Keep the separate tracker but reject overlap with the acknowledgement emoji and every configured status-reaction emoji.

options.title: Accept reaction interference
options.body: Allow overlapping custom emoji and explicitly document that one lifecycle may suppress another active signal.

recommendation.title: Extend status controller
recommendation.body: Use the canonical serialized source-message owner for subagent count, failure, and typing lifecycle alongside existing queued, thinking, tool, done, and error states.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared status-reaction lifecycle introduced in their merged feature is the canonical ownership surface this decision would extend.
